:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noMissingThrow`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- Sources: 
  - Inspired from [`oxc/missing-throw`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/oxc/missing-throw)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noMissingThrow": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow creating an error with `new` without throwing it.

Writing `new Error()` as a statement, without using its result, creates
an error object and then discards it. Nothing happens: the code keeps running as if no error
occurred. This is almost always a mistake where the `throw` keyword was
forgotten.

The rule checks constructors whose name starts with an uppercase letter
and ends with `Error`, such as `Error`, `TypeError`, or `ValidationError`.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
function check(value) {
    if (!value) {
        new Error("Missing value");
    }
}
```

### Valid

```js
function check(value) {
    if (!value) {
        throw new Error("Missing value");
    }
}

const createError = () => new Error("Something went wrong");

const error = new Error("Something went wrong");

reject(new Error("Something went wrong"));
```
